text:
ACT I

SCENE I. An open Place.

Thunder and Lightning. Enter three Witches.

FIRST WITCH.
When shall we three meet again?
In thunder, lightning, or in rain?

SECOND WITCH.
When the hurlyburly’s done,
When the battle’s lost and won.

THIRD WITCH. That will be ere the set of sun.

FIRST WITCH. Where the place?

SECOND WITCH. Upon the heath.

THIRD WITCH. There to meet with Macbeth.

FIRST WITCH. I come, Graymalkin!

SECOND WITCH. Paddock calls.

THIRD WITCH. Anon.

ALL.
Fair is foul, and foul is fair:
Hover through the fog and filthy air.

[Exeunt.]

reviewCriteria: Gloss the four target occurrences accurately in their dramatic context.
Retain the literal source; no reordered verse, merged speaker labels, or revised stage directions.
Allow the good/bad reversal in Fair is foul to remain a paradox; do not assert a single definitive interpretation.
Keep definitions short and age-appropriate; no invented character relationships or historical details.
Use essential for comprehension needs and helpful for enrichment; priority is a proposal, not a measure of literary quality.

variants.title: Explicit spelling stress test, not a second source edition
variants.derivation: Only Graymalkin is replaced with the alternate spelling Grimalkin; the canonical fixture remains unchanged.
